cards.title: PD Target Definition and Estimation
cards.claim: A PD target is a specific magnitude of a PK/PD index associated with a defined effect (e.g., stasis, 1-log kill, 2-log kill) relative to a specified baseline or comparator. Targets can be reported from literature or estimated from new data. Reported targets must retain their original index definition, units, free/total basis, and applicability context.
conditions: When defining a target for later PTA or regimen design.
When using a reported target from external literature.
required_inputs: Reference baseline (e.g., untreated control, start of therapy).
For estimation: Paired exposure-response observations with independent experimental unit identity.
For reported targets: Source, value, index definition, and uncertainty.
limitations: A published PD target is not automatically applicable to the target drug without context matching.
Stasis and log-kill targets are distinct; do not conflate.
Missing target definition is a gap, not a blocker for independent PK work.
cards.downstream_use: Input for PTA (Probability of Target Attainment) simulations.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
